hints: Notice the $30^{\circ}$ angle is measured from the dashed North line to the $75 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ arrow, so North is the adjacent side and East is the opposite side.
Recall that adjacent component is magnitude times cosine and opposite component is magnitude times sine of the given angle.
Compare $75 \cos 30^{\circ}$ for the northerly part with $75 \sin 30^{\circ}$ for the easterly part, then round to the table values in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given vector: magnitude $75 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $30^{\circ}$ east of North, with North vertical and East horizontal.
State the resolution rule: component along the angle - adjacent - is $v \cos \theta$, and component across the angle - opposite - is $v \sin \theta$.
Set up northerly component as adjacent to $30^{\circ}$: $v_N = 75 \cos 30^{\circ}$ and easterly component as opposite: $v_E = 75 \sin 30^{\circ}$.
Substitute values: $v_N = 75 \times 0.8660 \approx 64.95 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_E = 75 \times 0.5 = 37.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Round to the table precision: $v_N \approx 65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_E \approx 38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, with the larger component correctly on the North side closer to the arrow.
Match northerly $65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and easterly $38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the table. This is option C.

options.A: Northerly $38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ uses $75 \sin 30^{\circ}$ instead of $75 \cos 30^{\circ}$; the easterly $38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ alone is correct.
options.B: Values are swapped; $38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the easterly opposite-side component and $65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the northerly adjacent-side component.
options.C: Northerly $75 \cos 30^{\circ} \approx 65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and easterly $75 \sin 30^{\circ} = 37.5 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 38 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.D: Easterly $65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ uses $75 \cos 30^{\circ}$ instead of $75 \sin 30^{\circ}$; the northerly $65 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ alone is correct.
